[page[title]]

Expression-bodied methods must return awaitable calls directly instead of adding redundant async and await keywords.

What The Standard says

“Readability” — The Standard chooses readability over performative complexity. Returning an awaitable directly removes async and await when they add no control flow, mapping or exception boundary. read it here.
“efficient abstraction” — The Standard's asynchronous-abstraction guidance values clean and efficient awaitable APIs. The analyser removes redundant state-machine syntax while preserving the ValueTask contract. read it here.

Why it matters

When a method only returns an awaitable call, async and await add a state machine without adding behaviour. Returning the ValueTask directly keeps allocation and control flow minimal while accurately showing that the method delegates the operation.

Bad code example

// Violates STXFORMAT012: Expression-bodied methods must return awaitable calls directly instead of adding redundant async and await keywords.
async ValueTask<Student> GetStudentAsync() => await service.GetStudentAsync();

Good code example

// Follows STXFORMAT012
ValueTask<Student> GetStudentAsync() => service.GetStudentAsync();
